pitch: Build WordPress themes locally and ship them to staging and production through Claude Code — Git-backed, SSH-deployed, with no credentials in chat.
pitchMark: Build WordPress themes locally and ship them to staging and production
problem: You're building a WordPress theme and you want the developer-friendly flow — work locally, commit, push, watch CI/CD deploy to staging, smoke test, promote to prod. But wiring that up by hand is half a day of yak-shaving: Git remote, GitHub auth, SSH keys, GitHub Actions YAML, local WP config. And maintaining it across a dozen client projects is its own tax.

This skill makes the per-project setup about 30 minutes, then turns the everyday workflow basically chat-driven: build a block, ship to staging, promote to prod. Every production write stops for an explicit backup acknowledgement — there's no autopilot over your live site.

After setup, each project carries its own committed `.claude/` folder, so the next session — you, a teammate, or Claude — starts with full context: the CI/CD pattern in play, the conventions to follow (Sage or inherited), and the recent changelog.

callout.label: Backups are on you
callout.text: This skill **does not make backups**. Every production write — rsync, `wp db import`, `wp search-replace` — refuses to run without an explicit **"I have a backup"** acknowledgement. It assumes your host has automatic backups on, or that you take manual ones before destructive ops. **If you lose data, no skill can recover it.**

capabilities.label: What it does
capabilities.lede: It works in two modes — a new **Sage** build, or an **inherited** non-Sage theme it respects rather than rewrites. Setup is ~30 min per project; everyday work is chat-driven.

items.name: Scaffold a new Sage theme
items.desc: Roots Sage + Acorn + Blade + Tailwind v4 + Vite + Alpine + ACF Pro, wired to Git and CI/CD.

items.name: Work inside an inherited theme
items.desc: Respect the existing architecture; apply the core principles **without silently rewriting it**.

items.name: Build blocks, components & CPTs
items.desc: ACF blocks with previews, section/component/partial separation, the 3-layer CSS model.

items.name: Ship to staging & production
items.desc: Push to deploy via GitHub Actions, or rsync direct — smoke-tested, backup-gated.

items.name: Pull production down to local
items.desc: Copies the prod database and uploads to local with the URL search-replace done for you.

items.name: Carry project context in git
items.desc: A committed `.claude/` with CLAUDE.md, the CI/CD contract, and a rolling changelog travels with the code.

flow.d: ~30 min/project: local WP, Git, SSH, CI/CD pattern, .claude/ scaffold.
Edit locally to the Sage or inherited conventions — blocks, CPTs, sections.
Conventional Commit; CI/CD picks it up.
Deploys to staging; QA gate on the staging URL.
Tag a release → production deploy, gated by the backup prompt.
Appends [DEPLOY-PROD] to the project changelog and closes out.

commands: add a hero block with title, subtitle, and CTA fields
build a case-study CPT with an archive page
pull the production database to my local
what's the CI/CD pattern for this project?
rescan the architecture for this project

limits.label: What it won't do
items: **Make or restore backups** — every prod write gates on a backup you confirm; it never creates one.
**Manage content or ACF values** on a live site — that's the companion, `norml-wp-manager` (REST, no SSH).
**Introduce a new framework** on an inherited theme without asking — it matches what's already there.
**Fix a broken WordPress install** — corrupted database or core files go to your host.
**Security or penetration testing** — out of scope; use a dedicated tool.
limits.note: Local-first is the default. Direct-on-server edits are permitted but flagged **`[DIRECT-PROD]`** and logged, because the next deploy can overwrite them.
